prize_parts.citation: for the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, making the construction of aryl amines a predictable catalytic reaction

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange I keep palladium-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling as my single preferred part. The chair asks whether it is conceptually distinct from the 2010 prize. I think it is. The 2010 prize rewarded carbon-carbon coupling through transmetalation with organometallic partners. C-N coupling needs a different elementary step sequence: amine binding, formation of an amide-palladium intermediate, and a difficult C-N reductive elimination. That problem was solved by deliberate ligand design, first bidentate phosphines and then bulky electron-rich biaryl and ferrocenyl ligands, with mechanistic work behind each step. The citation can state this by saying 'general' and naming the arylamine bond. The discovery has been confirmed independently for about three decades and is used at scale in medicinal, process and materials chemistry. The Buchwald-Hartwig pair is also the only attribution on the shortlist that three members reached independently and that nobody has contested as the core. I would defend it on those merits, not on the count of first places, which is only three of eight.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection is still the 2010 overlap. A committee that sees C-N coupling as a downstream application of a recognised principle would reasonably decline it, and a second synthetic-methodology prize in a short period is a fair worry. Kosugi's and Migita's tin-amide couplings are real precursors, and I accept that the claim of the two ligand-design programmes is not free of dispute. I also accept that the unusually clean two-name allocation does not by itself make the field more important than targeted protein degradation or massively parallel sequencing, whose effect on biology and medicine is larger. My case is that it is the most secure on maturity, attribution and chemical content combined, not that it is the broadest in impact.

responses.point: Daniel prefers B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli, and treats the VHL and cereblon mechanisms as independently confirmed enough that a missing approved PROTAC drug should not delay recognition.
responses.response: I take the concept seriously and agree the mechanisms are confirmed. My concern remains that the field is two strands, PROTACs from Crews and Deshaies and cereblon glues from Handa and Ito. Your trio and Peter Brzezinski's trio differ in the third name, and that disagreement among its own supporters is a sign that the allocation is not settled. A prize that must choose between Ciulli and Handa has to explain why one strand of a joint field is left out. I also still weight the missing approval, since the claim of a new drug modality is stronger once a degrader is in routine clinical use. This did not change my ranking, but B026 stays my third choice and I would revisit it within a few years.

responses.point: Peter prefers B026 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, and notes that B065 would be the safer choice if the PROTAC and glue strands cannot be reconciled.
responses.response: I read your last point as an accurate statement of my own position. Handa's identification of cereblon is a very clean piece of mechanistic chemical biology, and it is the reason I would not cut the glue strand out of any later degrader prize. But your case against already says the trio may be two discoveries in one citation. If the committee cannot agree on a single citation wording today, the discovery that needs no such compromise is B065. I prefer to wait on B026 and not honour it with a split award.

responses.point: Johan argues that C-N coupling is a conceptual advance through amide-bound palladium intermediates and ligand-controlled reductive elimination, and not just an extension of the 2010 prize.
responses.response: I agree and I would like this reasoning in the citation, because it answers the chair's first question directly. I think the elementary-step argument is the best response to the 2010 overlap: the new problem was C-N reductive elimination, and ligand design solved it. On Kosugi we have also agreed that the general catalytic method is the credited achievement, so his earlier tin-amide work is a precursor mentioned in the record and does not make him a laureate. I do not see this point as a reason to add a third name.

responses.point: Heiner, as chair, asks whether massively parallel sequencing restricted to the Solexa chemistry and cluster readout can be accepted as chemistry, and whether the Balasubramanian and Klenerman pair settles the other claims.
responses.response: I agree with the two-name Solexa core and I am glad Mayer is no longer in your set. I still cannot say the Rothberg and Ju claims are settled by it, and Ju's reversible-terminator chemistry is chemically close to the Solexa route. As a heavy daily user I have a bias toward overrating the method, so I do not move it above B065, where nobody asks whether it is chemistry. If B065 does not reach five, B037 is my first alternative, and I would support the pair on that basis.

responses.point: Peter prefers B065 with Buchwald and Hartwig, notes Kosugi and Migita as precursors, and lists photoredox (B033) as an alternative.
responses.response: I agree that Kosugi and Migita belong in the citation context and not in the name list, since the three-name cap would otherwise exclude one of the two people who built the general method. I stay with my view that photoredox is a weaker pairing or substitute, because MacMillan's 2021 organocatalysis prize makes the credit awkward. On the chair's question about a two-part prize, I would not add a second part to B065. A single, clean achievement is easier to defend than a combination in which the second part needs compromises on credit.

uncertainties: Whether a majority of five accepts C-N coupling as distinct from the 2010 prize, which is the point on which the committee could turn against it.
Whether the Kosugi and Migita precursor work is adequately handled by the citation wording and not by adding a name.
Whether massively parallel sequencing is regarded as chemistry, and whether Rothberg and Ju claims are settled by the Solexa pair.
Whether the committee prefers to wait for a PROTAC approval, and which third name would hold for a later B026 award.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. My field of nucleotide metabolism and genome stability makes me a heavy user of massively parallel sequencing (B037, my first alternative), which I disclose as a possible bias. I have no personal or institutional tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or any other named candidate that would require recusal.
